info.title: AgriMinds AI-DREWS API
info.description:
AI-Enabled Drought Early Warning and Climate-Resilient Decision Support (AI-DREWS, Choke Mountain Watershed).

Sign in at `POST /api/v1/auth/login` and send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Every forecast response carries a `provenance` block describing the model version, training data source and issue month.

get.summary: Liveness: process is up (200 even when degraded)
Readiness: 503 until forecasts can be served

post.summary: Accept an invitation by setting a password
post.description: Unauthenticated, because the whole point is that the person has no password yet: the token is the credential. It works once and expires, and it grants nothing beyond setting the password on the one account it was issued for. Accepting signs the person in, so there is no second form asking for the password they just chose.

get.summary: Map geometry (public)
get.description: `watershed` is the surveyed catchment outline; `grid` is one polygon per forecast cell, keyed by `cell` (r{row}c{col}) so a BI tool can join it to a forecast. Geometry only: these carry no readings. Generate the grid with `ai-drews grid-geojson`.

post.summary: Ask for access (cooperative, office, insurer, ministry, NGO, university)
post.description:
The one unauthenticated write in the platform, and deliberately narrow. It records an enquiry and returns an acknowledgement — never whether the organisation is already a customer, because confirming that would turn a sales form into a directory of who pays.

An email address or a phone number is required: a lead nobody can reply to is not a lead. The segment is recorded as the enquirer's own description and is not binding; an administrator decides it on approval, because the price follows from it.

post.summary: An SMS, USSD or IVR turn arriving from the carrier
post.description:
Unauthenticated by design: the caller is a phone, not a session. An aggregator posts here and the signature header is what proves the post came from them, so `hotline_webhook_secret` must be set before the short code is public.

The reply is returned **and** recorded. With no aggregator connected it is recorded as `held`, never `sent`: a row marked sent when nothing left the building becomes a report claiming the hotline served farmers it never reached.

post.summary: Open a farmer account
post.description:
Creates the account as **pending**. A farmer's advisory is tied to a real holding in a real kebele and a form cannot prove either, so a development agent confirms it before the account can be signed into.

The acknowledgement is identical whether or not the number already has an account: saying otherwise would turn this form into a way to discover who is registered, one number at a time.

get.summary: Gridded drought probability for one lead
The surveyed catchment outline and which grid cells fall inside it
get.description: Lets a map draw the real catchment instead of a bare rectangle, and grey out the cells that are not part of it. The outline is simplified for display; the server keeps the full-precision version for deciding whether a plot is inside.

get.summary: Risk for one cell by row/col or GPS

get.summary: The full forecast horizon, and what each lead is worth
get.description: Every lead the model was trained for, each marked `forecast` or `outlook`. A forecast carries a probability and is published only where it was measured to beat climatology on held-out data; an outlook carries a direction and never a number. The measured skill travels with each lead so a client can show it rather than imply it.

post.summary: Crop advisory for a cell, lead and crop

get.summary: Niño 3.4 history and CNN-LSTM forecast
Predicted yield for every crop and altitude belt
get.description:
Yield in quintals per hectare for tef, wheat and maize across the Kolla, Woina Dega and Dega belts, conditioned on Niño 3.4 and on the last observed season.

Each cell also carries the same prediction with the ENSO anomaly removed, because the model leans overwhelmingly on last year's yield: the two numbers side by side are the whole of its climate response. Pass `lead_month` to condition on the platform's own ENSO forecast instead of the last observed month.

`year` defaults to the season after the crop record. The year is itself a fitted feature, so a year beyond the record adds no information — a gradient-boosted tree can only treat it as the last year it was trained on.

schema.description: Use the ENSO forecast at this lead instead of the last observation

post.summary: What-if: one crop and belt under named climate inputs
post.description: Anything left out falls back to the last observed season. The lag features are always the observed ones: this is a scenario over climate, not over history.

get.summary: Belt-average yields and Niño 3.4 across the record and beyond it
get.description:
The observed series plus one projected series per assumed ENSO state, in the shape a two-panel chart needs.

Observation is used wherever it exists. Niño 3.4 is measured several years past the end of the crop record, so the seasons in between are projected under the ENSO that actually happened and every scenario agrees there; only after `enso_observed_through` do they diverge. Nothing here forecasts ENSO beyond about six months (`enso_forecast_limit_months`), so those later years are assumptions, not predictions, and the response keeps the two labelled apart rather than drawing one line through both.

Each projected season is predicted from the one before it, because the lag features are inputs. The error compounds and the series converges on a level within a few steps.

get.summary: What El Niño years did to each crop and belt, measured over the record
get.description: A property of the 1990-2023 record rather than of the regressor: each crop-belt series is detrended, and El Niño years are compared with all other years by Welch's t-test. The response reports the effect, its p-value and the group sizes for every cell, so a reader can see where the record does and does not support a claim, and derives the per-belt recommendation from the same table.

get.summary: Scores for all five candidates, what the model leans on, and its limits
CNN-LSTM drought model performance metrics vs baselines
get.description:
Returns the full set of evaluation metrics produced at training time:

- **drought**: per-lead classification metrics for the drought model (AUC, Brier Score, BSS vs climatology, POD, FAR) with the persistence baseline AUC.
- **enso**: per-model regression metrics (RMSE, MAE, correlation) for the ENSO CNN-LSTM, a Persistence baseline, and a Ridge baseline, across all twelve leads.

These figures were measured once on held-out data at training time and are served unchanged. Nothing here is re-derived at request time.

post.summary: Decide a request
post.description:
Approving an organisation enquiry **creates the account and an account for its contact**, in the segment named here rather than the one the enquirer guessed. The link back is kept, so an account can always be traced to the enquiry it came from.

The response carries a single-use invitation token. There is no mail server here, so it is shown once and relayed to the contact by whoever approves -- it is not stored in readable form and re-reading the request will not return it.

get.summary: What every stakeholder pays
get.description:
The price in force for each of the eight stakeholder types, with every rate given both as integer cents and as a rendered decimal so a client never divides money itself.

Pass `include_history=true` to get superseded versions alongside the current ones. A price is never edited in place: changing one closes its window and opens a new row, so a subscription signed last year still resolves to the rate it was signed at.

post.summary: Issue an API key
post.description: The response carries the key itself, once. The platform stores only a SHA-256 hash and the last four characters, so it cannot show the key again and a stolen database does not hand anybody a working credential. Give it to the customer now or revoke and reissue.

delete.description: The row is kept: it is the record of what was issued and what it spent.

schema.title: Response Members Api V1 Organizations  Organization Id  Members Get

post.summary: Invite somebody to an account that already exists
post.description:
An organisation created directly — rather than through an access request — has no account anybody can sign in to. Neither does one approved from an enquiry that carried no email address. This is how either becomes reachable.

**No password is set.** The response carries a one-time link; the person chooses their own password at it. An administrator who could set it could then sign in as them, and nothing downstream could tell the two apart.

The link is shown once and only its hash is stored. A lost link is replaced by inviting again, not recovered.

get.summary: Institutional agreements on record
get.description: Individual farmer premiums are left out unless asked for: there is one per farmer, and a list that mixes them in with institutional licences stops being a list of accounts. They are counted in `/subscriptions/revenue` either way.

parameters.name: individuals

schema.description: Include farmers who bought premium themselves
schema.title: Individuals

parameters.description: Include farmers who bought premium themselves

schema.title: Response List Subscriptions Api V1 Subscriptions Get

post.summary: Record that an account agreed to a rate
post.description:
The rate is taken from the tier in force for the account's stakeholder type and **copied onto the agreement**, together with the tier version it came from. Repricing the catalogue afterwards therefore changes what new customers pay and leaves this one alone.

Supply `unit_price_cents` only for a negotiated price; leaving it out is the normal case and takes the list rate.

delete.description: The row is kept: it is what the account was charged for the term it ran.

get.summary: What the platform actually earns
get.description:
Counted from agreements that are live on the day asked about — not from the price list. The catalogue total on the pricing page is what one of everything would fetch if it all sold; this is what is owed.

A perpetual licence contributes **nothing** to ARR, because it recurs never. Its one-off value is reported separately so it cannot be mistaken for recurring revenue.

post.summary: Ask the farmer agent a question
post.description:
Answers from **this farmer's own plots** and the forecast for them. The agent chooses which of the advisory engine's findings answers the question; it does not compose agronomic advice of its own, so it cannot state a planting date the model never produced.

A digit works as well as a sentence — `1` is the drought risk — because the same agent answers the USSD menu on the hotline.

When the forecast is unavailable the agent says so rather than answering from a stale number.

get.summary: What the hotline has been asked lately
get.description: Newest first. `delivered` is false for every row until a carrier is connected, and `registered` false means a farmer the platform has not reached asked it something — which is the most useful column here.

schema.title: Response Recent Api V1 Admin Hotline Get

get.summary: Who is waiting to be confirmed
get.description: Oldest first: somebody who signed up a week ago is the one being kept waiting.

schema.title: Response Pending Api V1 Staff Signups Get

post.summary: Register a farmer who is standing in front of you
post.description:
For the farmer who walks into the office or meets the agent in the field — the case the hotline points at when it tells an unregistered caller to ask their development agent.

Approved immediately, because the check the queue performs has just been done in person. **No password is set here**: the response carries a one-time link and the farmer chooses their own, so no staff member ends up holding a credential that signs in as a farmer.

post.summary: Confirm or refuse a sign-up
post.description: Open to any staff member, not only an administrator: the person who can actually say whether a holding exists is the development agent for that woreda. Who decided and when is recorded on the account.

post.summary: Issue a password reset link
post.description:
There is no email and no SMS carrier to send a reset to, so the channel is the person who can already identify the farmer: their development agent.

The link is shown once and only its hash is stored, so it cannot be looked up again — a lost link is replaced, not recovered. Issuing one also spends any link the account already held, so this revokes whatever was outstanding.

get.summary: The plans this account can choose from
get.description: Only the caller's own segment, because the price follows from it and a cooperative cannot buy at a research rate. Periods the tier does not sell are left out rather than shown as free, and each option carries what a year on it costs so the terms can be compared on one scale.

post.summary: Choose a plan
post.description:
Creates the subscription as **pending payment** and issues an invoice against a reference to quote on a bank transfer. No money moves through this platform: the plan starts when an administrator confirms the payment, not when this call returns.

The price is frozen at the moment of choosing, so a catalogue change between choosing and paying cannot restate the bill.

get.summary: This account's bills

schema.title: Response My Invoices Api V1 Plans Invoices Get

get.summary: Everything still unpaid, soonest due first

schema.title: Response Outstanding Api V1 Admin Invoices Get

post.summary: Confirm a payment arrived
post.description: Settles the bill and starts the subscription it paid for.

post.summary: Sell an account a bundle of advisory messages
post.description: Credits are priced per message and the rate is frozen on the bundle, so a later price change cannot restate a sale that already happened.

get.summary: Credits bought, spent and left
get.description:
Derived on every read from the bundles and the deliveries, never stored, so the figure cannot drift from the rows that justify it. A failed message is not charged for.

`deliverable` is false while no aggregator is configured: messages are recorded and queued, and nothing is actually sent.

post.summary: Queue one advisory for delivery
post.description: Refused with 409 when the account has no credits left.

diverge, which is where `scenarios` stops agreeing with itself.

HorizonResponse.title: HorizonResponse
HorizonResponse.description:
The full horizon: what can be forecast, what can only be leaned on, and why.

The split is the point. A forecast says how likely drought is and is published only where
that was measured to beat climatology. An outlook says which way the season leans and never
carries a number. Serving the second as the first is the failure this endpoint prevents.

OrganizationEnquiry.title: OrganizationEnquiry
OrganizationEnquiry.description:
The public form. No account exists yet, so everything is self-reported.

The contact chooses their own password here, exactly as a farmer does at sign-up. Nothing is
usable until an administrator approves: the account is created `pending`, and approval is what
turns a self-reported claim into an account somebody can sign in to.

Asking for it here rather than relaying a link afterwards removes a step that existed only
because there is no mail server -- and a step where a credential was read down a phone.
